problem: score_area_for_finding (src/output/json/helpers.rs) decided which accessibility score area a finding belonged to by lowercasing rule_id + title + description + subcategory into one string and running word-prefix matching over it, even though every finding already carries structured taxonomy data. A near-verbatim duplicate of the same logic lived in score_area_for_key_point (src/output/builder/single/executive.rs) for the executive driver note, so each misclassification had to be fixed twice or silently was not. The function was also applied to every finding regardless of category, letting SEO findings drive areas of the accessibility breakdown.
evidence: reports/inros-lackner-audit.json generated 2026-09-19 (auditmysite v1.5.0): a11y.landmark_region.missing, whose description reads "Element with role 'image' is not contained within a landmark region", was published under area "Images / alternative text" as its main_driver with 15 occurrences — the `image` branch is evaluated before the `landmark` branch, so a word inside the description of a landmark rule won. In the same report seo.headings.multiple_h1 (category "seo") was the main_driver of the "Heading structure" area of accessibility_score_breakdown. Three earlier instances of the same class are recorded separately: score-area-substring-misclassification, score-area-form-conformance-word-boundary-misclassification and score-area-navigation-subcategory-misclassification.
expected: The area must be read from the taxonomy, not from prose. taxonomy::score_area::RULE_AREAS maps every accessibility rule_id to a ScoreArea explicitly; score_area_for_finding looks the rule up there and returns None for any finding whose category is not "wcag", so the breakdown describes the same population as accessibility_score. score_area_for_key_point delegates to the same function instead of keeping a second copy. The text-matching helpers key_has_word_starting_with and strip_css_selector_spans are deleted.
counter_examples: a11y.bypass_blocks.missing and a11y.landmark_main.missing must still classify as "Landmarks / page structure", and a11y.alt_text.missing as "Images / alternative text" — the mapping must not over-correct the cases that were already right; see score_area_still_classifies_real_findings.

A finding whose rule_id is not in the rule register at all (dynamically produced rules) still falls back to score_area_for_subcategory. That path is deliberately coarse and is unreachable for registered rules, which the totality test enforces.
